Hybrid/Remote.

title: Legal Associate
description:
About Ornn

Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.


About the Role

Working directly with Ornn's counsel, you would review and mark up MSAs, order forms and service level agreements, track what is outstanding, and keep contracts moving. Most of it is careful, methodical work on standard paper.

This is a role for someone with real legal training who would rather see how commercial contracts work at a company building a new market than review the hundredth version of the same document at a firm.


What You'll Do

  • Review and redline customer MSAs, order forms and service level agreements against our standard positions.

  • Prepare first drafts, and turn counsel's comments into clean language.

  • Track every contract in flight: which version is current, whose turn it is, and how long it has been sitting.

  • Support supplier paperwork: NDAs, diligence documents and onboarding.

  • Take contract questions off the go-to-market team so they can sell.

Requirements

  • A JD, a paralegal certificate, or late-stage enrollment in a law program. This role needs real legal training, not an adjacent degree.

  • Experience reviewing commercial contracts, or clear evidence you can pick it up quickly.

  • Precise and methodical. In this job the detail is the work.

  • Able to run a queue and chase people without being asked twice.

  • Discreet with confidential commercial terms.

  • Based in New York and able to work in person at our office.


Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with technology, services or infrastructure contracts, particularly MSAs and service level agreements.

  • Time in an in-house legal team at a startup rather than only at a firm.

  • Interest in commercial or commodity markets, or in how compute is becoming an asset class.

  • Familiarity with DocuSign and contract management tools.


Why This Role Matters

Ornn sells capacity it does not own, under contracts that promise availability and delivery dates. When our customer paper and our supplier paper do not line up, we carry the difference. Catching that at review is far cheaper than discovering it at a service credit. This role is how the paper keeps up with the deal flow, and how the rest of the team stops doing legal work on the side.


Compensation and Benefits

Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, free meals, and additional benefits. This is an early role with significant impact and equity upside.


Equal Opportunity Statement

Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

title: Data Analyst (Billing)
description:
About FunnelFox

FunnelFox is a complete growth solution for subscription apps. With visibility across 1,000+ apps and $2B in processed revenue, our growth agent shows you how to get your next 10x, and our platform gives you everything to make it happen: AI-built web2app funnels, analytics, A/B testing and our own payments infrastructure.

About the role

As FunnelFox grows, so does the complexity of our data.

We’re building our analytics foundation with our own data warehouse, dbt, and Airflow. Now we’re looking for a strong analyst who can turn messy source data into trusted business logic, clear marts, and usable dashboards.

You’ll work closely with our Analytics Lead and Data Engineer, primarily across Billing & Payments. Your work will power both internal decision-making and client-facing reporting, so accuracy and trust in data are critical.

Your main focus will be the business layer of analytics: marts, metric logic, and datasets behind reporting. You won’t own ingestion or raw-layer pipelines, but you should be comfortable investigating source systems, identifying gaps, and defining clear upstream requirements.

This is an IC role for someone comfortable with ambiguity and building analytics while the system itself is still evolving.

What you’ll do

  • Own analytical problems end to end: turn ambiguous business questions into trusted analytical results.

  • Define and validate metric logic: establish how key metrics are calculated, reconcile results against source systems, and prevent misleading numbers from reaching stakeholders or clients.

  • Bring structure to messy data: investigate APIs, source tables, and existing reporting logic to understand what is useful, missing, or unreliable.

  • Build business-facing marts: own the analytical logic behind datasets used for dashboards, reporting, and decision-making.

  • Shape upstream engineering requirements: define what needs to change when raw data or lower-layer models don’t support reliable analytics.

  • Improve analytics consistency: reduce duplicated logic and dashboard drift through reusable datasets, clear ownership, and documentation.

  • Partner across the business: work closely with the Analytics Lead, Data Engineer, Product, CS, Marketing, and Finance.

What we’re looking for

  • Strong SQL and analytical thinking: you can explore messy data, validate logic, spot edge cases, and build reliable datasets.

  • Strong ownership and metric sense: you can work from vague questions, define meaningful metrics, compare methodologies, and explain discrepancies.

  • Broad analytics experience: you’ve worked across product, business, or revenue analytics — including product usage, funnels, operational, reporting, or financial metrics.

  • Experience with dbt or a close equivalent: you understand modular modeling, marts, dependencies, and maintainable business logic.

  • Ability to work across B2B and B2C logic: from customer-level business metrics to end-user or lead behavior.

  • Ability to translate data complexity into engineering requirements: you can identify what needs to change upstream and explain why.

  • High standards for data quality and collaboration: you validate outputs, document assumptions, and work effectively across technical and business teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience in B2B SaaS and client-facing reporting

  • Experience with billing, payments, subscriptions, invoices, refunds, or reconciliation

  • Experience with product analytics and behavioral data

  • Experience with systems thinking or data systems design

  • Experience working with API data structures and Data Engineers on warehouse design

  • ClickHouse experience

What you may expect from working with us:

  • Flexible remote work: Work from anywhere with a schedule that fits your life. Our core team operates in Europe, and we welcome candidates worldwide using .

  • High ownership and real impact: You’ll actively influence product and technical decisions, not just execute predefined tasks.

  • Fast-moving startup environment: We value speed, autonomy, and practical problem-solving over rigid corporate processes.

  • Direct communication: We keep things simple and transparent, ensuring you focus on what matters most — getting things done.

  • Professional Support: We provide a monthly budget that you can allocate based on your personal and professional priorities — including language learning, professional development, mental health support, sports, or health insurance.

title: Engineering Program Manager, NPD
description:
About Turtlebox Audio

The first Turtlebox was born out of necessity. After breaking every “loud” product on the market through routine outdoor use, the idea of the Turtlebox was born in our garage, not as a business but just for personal use. Nothing else could get the job done.

Most portable speakers aren’t actually meant for the outdoors and can’t withstand the elements, the ones that can aren’t loud enough to be heard. When you’re at the beach or on an ATV, you need sound to carry in order to hear it over the wind, waves, and boat engines, you need a Turtlebox.

We soon realized that there was a huge need for the Turtlebox among likeminded adventurers and our journey began to set out to make the world’s loudest most rugged outdoor portable speaker.

Click here for a peek inside our workplace!

Role Overview:

Turtlebox's mission is to engineer the most durable, loudest, and premium sounding speakers on the market. Bringing that to life takes organization, products don't ship unless someone is watching the clock, tracking every open action, and making sure the right people are talking to each other at the right time.

We're looking for a Project Manager who thrives in that role. This position reports to the Product Director. You own the schedule. You run the cross-functional rhythm. You know when something is off track before the team does, and you know how to move people without friction — because you've built enough trust and credibility that when you ask for a status or flag a risk, people respond. You're not here to babysit; you're here to make a high-performing team even more effective by taking the coordination burden off them so they can do the work they're best at.

This is a hub-of-communication role. Every active development program runs through you. Engineering, Industrial Design, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product all count on you to keep the program visible, the blockers surfaced, and the schedule honest.

Key Responsibilities:

Own the Program — Schedule, Budget, and Risk

  • Build and maintain master project schedules for all active NPD programs — from kick-off through EVT, DVT, PVT, and launch; keep them current and surface schedule impacts immediately when reality changes
  • Define milestones, task dependencies, and critical path items in collaboration with functional leads
  • Track program costs against budget — tooling, NRE, third-party testing, and other program spend — and flag variances early
  • Maintain a live risk register for every active program — document risks, assess probability and impact, own the mitigation plan, and always be a few steps ahead of the next problem

Run the Cross-Functional Rhythm

  • Own the weekly cross-functional project cadence — run efficient meetings, capture decisions and actions, and follow up until they're closed
  • Track all open action items across Engineering, ID, Quality, and Supply Chain — know what's on track, what's slipping, and what needs escalation
  • Prepare clear, accurate project status updates for leadership — no spin, just the facts on where things stand
  • Drive Gate Reviews — build the agenda, prepare the status package, run the session, and give leadership a straight read on where the program stands, what's at risk, and what decisions need to be made

Drive Accountability Without Authority

  • Hold every function accountable to their commitments — with persistence, professionalism, and the credibility that comes from knowing the details
  • Push the team to produce their best work without adding unnecessary pressure — you know when to apply heat and when to remove a blocker
  • Escalate quickly and clearly when something is blocked and can't be resolved at the working level
  • Never let a missed task or an unclear owner slide — every action has a name and a date

Be the Communication Hub

  • Serve as the connective tissue across Engineering, ID, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management on every active program
  • Make sure information flows to the people who need it — proactively, not reactively
  • Maintain a single source of truth for project status, timelines, decisions, and open items
  • Keep stakeholders informed without burying them — good communication is clear, concise, and timely

Build and Improve the Process

  • Develop and refine the stage-gate process for NPD programs as the team and product line scale
  • Identify recurring bottlenecks and systemic gaps in how programs are run — propose and implement improvements
  • Build templates, tools, and tracking systems that give the team visibility without adding administrative burden

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline or Business — Engineering, Physics, Supply Chain, Operations Management, or related field
  • 5+ years of experience in an engineering program management role within a hardware product development environment
  • Demonstrated track record managing complex, cross-functional NPD programs through EVT, DVT, PVT, and production launch
  • Exceptional organizational skills — you manage multiple programs simultaneously without dropping anything
  • Natural communicator who can adapt to engineers, designers, factory partners, and executives in the same day
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-moving priorities — you create structure where it doesn't exist
  • Firm but collaborative — you get people to deliver without burning relationships
  • Detail-oriented at the task level, but always tracking the big picture
  • Proficient with project management tools — MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira, or equivalent

Preferred Experience:

  • PMP certification or equivalent formal project management training
  • Experience in consumer electronics, audio, or outdoor/ruggedized product development
  • Familiarity with hardware development stage-gate processes and build phases (EVT/DVT/PVT)
  • Experience coordinating with contract manufacturers or offshore suppliers
  • Background managing programs that involve regulatory certification timelines

Work Environment and Physical Requirements:

  • This position involves working in a traditional work environment, 5 days a week
  • Occasional lifting and carrying of up to 30lbs
  • Able and willing to travel 10%, including internationally, for supplier audits and build support

Why Join Turtlebox?:

  • Be part of a fast-growing premium outdoor audio brand with strong momentum in wholesale and D2C.
  • Coworkers who are as passionate about music and adventure as you are.
  • Thrive in an entrepreneurial culture with room for creativity, ownership, and innovation.
  • Complimentary lunch every day.
  • 12 annual holidays plus Paid Time Off.
  • Comprehensive health benefits & 401k matching.
  • Awesome discounts to complete your Turtlebox collection!

About Ornn

Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.


About the Role

Almost all of the capacity Ornn sells is build-to-order. A customer signs for nodes that do not exist yet, a supplier cuts a purchase order with the OEM, and somewhere between that order and a working cluster the schedule slips. When it slips it is a problem for the customer, a problem for us, and under many of our contracts it carries steep delay penalties.

You would own the deployment track end to end: one person, one process, asking suppliers the right question at the right time, and seeing a delay far enough out that we can still do something about it.


What You'll Do

  • Own the schedule for every build-to-order deployment, from purchase order to nodes in service.

  • Run a standing cadence with suppliers: demand forecasting with the OEM, an All Parts In date, weekly component checks, a firm ship date, then build, validation and shipment.

  • Track the components that actually move dates

  • Track facility readiness in parallel: power, cooling, site works, construction and anything on site that can push a date.

  • Escalate early. Surface a slip while there is still room to act, with the delay penalty exposure attached.

  • Hand off cleanly to fleet operations when capacity goes live, and report the actual in-service date, since invoicing and revenue recognition run off it.

  • Build the process and the tooling as you go. There is a tracker today and not much else.

Requirements

  • 2+ years in technical program management, project management, deployment or supply chain, in hardware, data centers or infrastructure.

  • Experience holding external vendors to a schedule, and escalating before a date is missed rather than after.

  • Comfortable with the technical detail. You do not need to design a cluster, but you need to know what a missing NIC does to a ship date.

  • Short, clear written updates. People should be able to read your status in ten seconds.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Data center build or GPU cluster deployment experience.

  • Familiarity with OEM and ODM lead times and component allocation.

  • Exposure to liquidated damages, service levels or delivery terms in commercial contracts.

  • Time at a neocloud, data center operator, systems integrator or hardware manufacturer.


Why This Role Matters

Ornn's customer contracts carry target delivery dates with real money behind them. Every deployment that lands late costs us penalties, credibility with that customer, and usually the next deal with them. Nobody owns that timeline today, which is exactly why this role exists. Done well, it turns delivery from something we find out about into something we manage.


Compensation and Benefits

Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, free meals, and additional benefits.


Equal Opportunity Statement

Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

AI Knowledge Readiness

title: Due Diligence Engineer
description:
About Ornn

Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.


About the Role

Today the technical review of a new operator gets split across people who already have other jobs, which makes it both a bottleneck on bringing supply onto the platform and the place a lot of our risk quietly sits.

You would own that review. When our supply team brings in a new operator, you are the person who reads the documentation and says whether the site is what it claims to be: racks and elevations, topology, power and cooling, heat exchangers, chassis, fiber and the network path. Then you run the process from there, chasing the gaps and driving to a yes or no rather than handing a list of questions to someone else.

You'll work alongside the supply team, who bring the operator in, and finance, who run the commercial side of the same review. The technical judgment is yours.


What You'll Do

  • Run the technical and IT review of every new supplier site: racks, topology, power and cooling, heat exchangers, chassis, cabling and network path.

  • Read operator documentation critically and find what is missing, not just what is there.

  • Project manage diligence end to end, chasing operators for the documents and answers you need and closing to a decision.

  • Set the standard for what an operator has to produce to get listed on Ornn, and tighten it as we learn.

  • Flag where a site's real capability does not match the service levels we are about to promise a customer.

  • Work with the supply team on new operators and with finance on commercial and financial diligence.

  • Stay close to capacity after it is signed, because what you find in diligence is what deployment and fleet operations inherit.

Requirements

  • Hands-on experience with data center infrastructure: power, cooling, racks, structured cabling and network topology.

  • Able to read site documentation, single line diagrams, rack elevations and network diagrams and tell whether they hold up.

  • Comfortable running a process, not only doing the review: owning the timeline, chasing people, closing items out.

  • Clear, direct writing. Your review has to be something a commercial team can act on.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Time at a neocloud, colocation provider, data center developer or hyperscaler, doing site reviews, commissioning or deployments.

  • A mechanical or electrical engineering background, or deep enterprise IT infrastructure experience.

  • Familiarity with GPU cluster builds, InfiniBand fabrics and liquid cooling.

  • Vendor or site due diligence in a commercial setting, where the output was a decision rather than a report.

  • Exposure to infrastructure or private equity diligence processes.


Why This Role Matters

Ornn promises customers availability on capacity it does not own. That promise is made at diligence, not at deployment. Every service credit we pay, every late deployment and every penalty traces back to something a site review either caught or missed. This role is the gate, and today the gate is a few people doing it between other jobs.


Compensation and Benefits

Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, free meals, and additional benefits. This is a senior role with significant impact and equity upside.


Equal Opportunity Statement

Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

title: Facilities Assistant
description:
Location: 25N Coworking in Schaumburg, IL

Who are we?

25N Coworking was created to usher in the changing work landscape. We are a fast-moving, rapidly growing organization that specializes in hospitality-forward coworking spaces and

best-in-class workspace design. We are pioneers in the flex workspace industry, and are powered by the dynamic, forward-thinking, and community-oriented team members that are the face of our company. Together, we’re changing the way we work.

Schedule + Availability:

This full-time role works about 40 hours per week. Working hours will fall during the day Monday-Friday. Some exceptions will apply for occasional evening and weekend events, with the ability to flex time to accommodate meeting and event schedule needs.

Your daily objective:

As our Coworking Porter, you’ll be responsible for maintaining the cleanliness and appearance of our space, and generally ensuring common areas are kept tidy and well-maintained. We also host many meetings and events in our space, that you’ll have facilities oversight for, which includes setting up and breaking down event spaces, moving furniture, equipment, and supplies, ensuring the venue is prepared for events by arranging tables, chairs, stages, and decorations, often requiring physical labor like lifting heavy items, all while maintaining a clean and organized environment and providing customer service to members and guests; essentially working behind the scenes to facilitate our coworking, meeting and event business. Some specifics of the day-to-day responsibilities include:

Member + Event General Support:

  • Responding to event-related requests and addressing minor issues
  • Greeting visitors and providing general guidance within the space
  • Assisting with guest flow and directing attendees
  • Responding to member and guest requests and concerns related to the facilities and services
  • Open + close the space when needed, and related responsibilities

Event setup:

  • Moving and arranging tables, chairs, stages, and other event furniture
  • Setting up audio-visual equipment
  • Hanging signs and decorations
  • Preparing catering areas
  • Set up coffee/water stations with beverages, cups and related supplies

Event breakdown:

  • Disassembling event setups
  • Removing and storing furniture and equipment
  • Cleaning up + re-staging the rooms until their next event

Handy-Person:

  • Minor repairs like paint touch-ups, replacing light bulbs, adjusting drawer or door hinges, repairing table legs or chairs, changing water filters, hanging pictures, etc.
  • Maintaining and restocking kitchen, meeting room, copy room, bathroom or other supplies
  • Inspecting for potential maintenance issues and reporting them to the appropriate personnel

Cleaning & Ensuring a Magazine-Ready Space:

  • Vacuum or sweep floors
  • Emptying trash cans and recycling bins
  • Wiping down furniture and surfaces
  • Loading/emptying the dishwasher and hand-washing dishes when needed
  • Cleaning and tidying the bathroom
  • Spot cleaning as needed

What we’re looking for:

  • Physical ability: Able to perform repetitive and/or physical tasks, like moving tables and chairs, lifting heavy objects, standing/walking for extended periods (specifics below).
  • Basic “Handy-person” skills: Ability to operate basic mechanical equipment, maintenance skills and ability to troubleshoot minor issues.
  • Attention to detail: Ensure specific cleanliness and organizational standards, and ensuring event setups are precise and on brand.
  • Teamwork: Collaborating with other 25N staff to maintain “Magazine-Readiness” of the space and execute event setups efficiently.
  • Flexibility + Independence: Adapting to changing space and event requirements, paired with ability to facilitate meeting schedules and overall workspace needs.
  • Customer service skills: Responding to member and guest needs and providing assistance with a positive attitude

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS (these are essential for this role, but let us know if you have questions or have an accommodation request):

  • Lift and carry up to 40 lbs.
  • Move furniture, equipment, etc. up to 100 lbs with assistance. For example, move a desk with the help of a dolly and/or a co-worker.
  • Ascend and descend ladders and stairs.
  • Regularly access low/high spaces that may be at irregular angles, such as under a desk or high shelves.
  • Operate computer and office equipment, including coffee maker, water filters/machines, laptop, mouse, copy machine, meeting room equipment and similar.
  • Be standing and walking for most of the day with 2-3 breaks per day.
  • Maintain concentration and focus in a busy environment where people are coming and going.
  • Work in loud, chaotic environments and/or in crowds during community events.

Pay + Benefits:

  • Hourly pay rate, $18 per hour.
  • Healthcare benefits, including medical, dental, vision, short & long term disability, and life insurance
  • Paid Vacation Time
  • 5 paid sick days per year
  • 11 paid holidays per year
  • 2 days of paid volunteer time per year
  • $1,000 annual stipend for ongoing training, wellness, and education, after 6 months of service
  • Gorgeous, expertly-designed workspace with access to 25N Coworking’s stunning amenities
  • A team culture of support and inclusivity.
  • Bottomless fresh-roasted coffee, tea, and filtered water to power your workday.
  • Loads of 25N-branded swag, like free water bottles, t-shirts, and stickers
  • …did we mention snacks?

title: Product Engineer, Full Stack
description:
Machines learned to understand language. We’re teaching them to understand matter.

Forty percent of global manufacturing happens through physical and chemical processes inside pipes, tanks, and reactors. Despite decades of industrial automation, much of what happens inside them remains remarkably invisible. Manufacturing is the most ubiquitous and foundational sector in global economy, yet the way factories are fundamentally run have used the same control philosophies, manual operations, and legacy software for the past 60 years.

Laminar deploys state-of-the-art patented sensors and edge hardware directly into live production environments, generating data that didn’t previously exist to build foundation models deployed in factory floors that understand chemistry, composition, quality, and material state in real time. We use that understanding to run autonomy and rethink how things are made.

The last generation of industrial automation taught machines to execute instructions reliably. The next will teach them to understand the processes they control and run autonomously, adaptively, and agentically: higher quality, safety, more efficiently, sustainably, and productively.

That future is already taking shape. Today, Laminar works with 7 of the world’s 10 largest food and beverage manufacturers and operates across hundreds of factories globally across six continents. Our systems have materially reduced waste, cut manufacturing downtime, saved water, chemicals, energy, and helped prevent safety and quality failures. Our technology has gained international recognition, from being selected as a 2026 World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer, Gold 2026 Edison Award, Unilever Startup of the Year, to Innovator Awards by both Coca-Cola and AB InBev, and more.

We are backed by tier-one investors in physical AI to make intelligent, self-improving production the new standard for industry.

Join us to build what makes matter intelligible, and the intelligible controllable.

The Role

Laminar Insights is where the plant sees what Laminar did and why. Every Laminar Line streams sub-second telemetry into it: what the sensors saw, what the model decided, and what each run saved in time, water, chemicals, and energy. A factory operator uses it to watch production in progress. A plant manager uses it to defend savings to corporate. An executive uses it to see how their manufacturing footprint is performing. Insights is the platform that makes that telemetry usable. Here’s a short explainer video on Insights:

We are looking for engineers who understand the bigger picture and work across the stack: frontend, backend, design, and everything in between to create great products that users love – all the way from customers to forward deployed engineers (FDEs).

  • Some broad questions that we are currently thinking deeply about:
  • How does Insights pull narratives and trends out of factory operations data?
  • How should the interface adapt to each facility's processes?
  • How do we represent Laminar's impact at a plant accurately?
  • How can we build internal products that are force multipliers for our FDEs?

What You Will Do

  • Collaborate with data science, backend, forward deployed engineering teams to ideate, collect feedback, prototype and productionize solutions on Insights that address challenges our customers are facing.
  • Work with different customer profiles to build Insights functionalities for their personas and ensure end to end delivery and success of features built.
  • Work with engineers, FDEs and leadership to identify friction points and build internal products that help FDEs move quickly, achieve customer goals, and understand the Laminar model stack.
  • Deliver polished user-facing features with scalable UI components that help increase the interpretability of our ML models, add more observability into the processes running in our customers' factories, and more.
  • Write clean, efficient, and well-documented code
  • Always be on the lookout for how to improve application performance by adopting latest innovations in frontend frameworks, optimizing SQL queries, or refactoring backend API calls.

About You

  • 1-4 years of experience working with customer-facing products.
  • Strong proficiency in React/Typescript and experience working with modern frontend tooling.
  • Familiarity with Python for data visualizations, rapid prototyping
  • Strong UX sensibilities and enthusiasm about building features that are performant, intuitive, and polished
  • A self-driven, high ownership mentality to first, conceptualize the needs of customers with very different business needs and then, shipping solutions to production.
  • An appreciation for simplicity and pragmatism when building software.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively in a collaborative in-person office in Boston.

Benefits

  • Direct impact on product and culture.
  • Comprehensive benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Disability, Transportation benefit, Health and Wellness benefit, and more.
  • 401k plan with employer matching
  • Equity
  • Competitive salary and bonus opportunities.
  • Dynamic and inclusive work environment.
  • Opportunities for growth and professional development.
  • Access to Greentown Labs' extensive network of cleantech startups.
  • Transportation benefit for your commute
  • A team that celebrates together from rooftop lunches, ping pong matches, Lunch & Learns, and regular team events

Learn How We Think

  • Learn about our startup journey: Our Journey
  • How we're combating climate change: AI-Powered Climate Tech
  • A customer story: Unilever uses Laminar precision automation to cut time & water usage
There are many easier places to work on AI. Laminar is for people who want the hardest version of their discipline. Models here must survive contact with physics. Hardware must survive years of continuous industrial operation. Software must integrate with machinery built decades ago. Everything we build ultimately has to work on a factory floor.
We believe exceptional people should be given exceptional amounts of ownership. At Laminar, you will have the context to form your own view, the permission to challenge ours, and the resources to pursue the right answers, whatever technical or organizational boundaries stand in the way. There are few layers between identifying something important and changing it.
We’re fortunate to work with a small polymathic team of hardware and software engineers, chemists, AI researchers, factory operators, and go-to-market wizards who are unusually capable, curious, rigorous, ambitious, and low-ego. If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.

Our Interview Process
1. Phone screen with Laminar HR/Recruiter (15-20 minutes)
2. Intro call with Hiring Manager (30 minutes)
3. On-site interview, overview of tech, and interview/presentation with the Hiring Manager and a few team members. Depending on the role, a skills exercise that should take no longer than an hour to prep, would be sent ahead of time. We record your skills exercise to share with any team members who could not join the interview and/or with Founder's ahead of their Founder's Interview. If you are not local, we can conduct this virtually.
4. Finalists for Full-Time positions will have a Founder’s Interview in-person

title: Director, Security Engineering (Application & Cloud Security)
description:
Uniphore is the Business AI company. Our sovereign, composable and secure AI platform connects enterprise data, fine-tunes AI models and deploys agentic AI across the enterprise. We empower every worker to boost productivity and help businesses grow faster, operate smarter and reduce costs. Trusted by more than 2,000 businesses globally, and recognized on the Deloitte Fast 500, Uniphore delivers on the promise of AI as a transformative force for business.


Job Description:

Uniphore is an AI company building agentic AI systems for the world’s largest enterprises. Our customers are banks, insurers, healthcare providers, and telecoms who hand us their most sensitive conversations and processes. Security is not a compliance exercise here. It is a condition of every deal we close.

We are hiring a Director of Security Engineering to own application and cloud security across the company and to build the security engineering practice for autonomous AI agents. As Uniphore moves from conversational AI to agents that carry out multi-step business processes on a customer’s behalf, the security problem shifts from protecting data at rest to protecting what an agent is allowed to decide, invoke, and act on.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will lead a distributed engineering team, work daily with product engineering, and be the person the Head of Information Security and the executive team rely on to say whether a given architecture is defensible.

What You Will Do

Secure the agentic AI platform

  • Own the multi-year security roadmap for our AI products, including agent workflows, MCP, RAG pipelines, and AI-enabled services.

  • Define and drive runtime security controls to protect against prompt injection, goal hijacking, unauthorized tool calls, data exfiltration, and other emerging AI threats.

  • Own the security architecture for agent sandboxing and isolated execution, ensuring untrusted code and tool outputs cannot impact the host environment or other tenants.

  • Build and lead a continuous AI red-team program focused on model, agent, and AI application security, including adversarial testing, data poisoning, model abuse, and privacy risks.

Own cloud and infrastructure security

  • Define and enforce cloud security standards across AWS, GCP, and Azure, including requirements for protecting sensitive customer data and supporting zero-data-retention commitments.

  • Establish secure identity and access models for workloads and AI agents, ensuring least-privilege access across cloud environments.

  • Drive Infrastructure-as-Code security and cloud security posture management to maintain a consistent security posture across global environments.

  • Partner with Security Operations, Engineering, and Cloud teams to improve cloud monitoring, detection, vulnerability management, and incident response.

Build the paved road for engineering

  • Build and drive an automated security toolchain integrated into CI/CD, covering application security testing, open-source dependencies, infrastructure, containers, and threat modeling.

  • Turn security and compliance requirements, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001, into automated technical controls wherever possible.

  • Partner with Engineering leadership to define and maintain the security bar for products and infrastructure.

  • Establish risk-based remediation priorities so engineering teams focus on the vulnerabilities and exposures that matter most.

Lead the team

  • Report directly to the Head of Information Security and serve as a senior security leader across AI, product, cloud, and infrastructure security.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, AI/R&D, Cloud, Infrastructure, and Compliance leadership to embed security into the development and delivery lifecycle.

  • Mentor and develop security engineers and emerging security leaders, helping them grow their technical, strategic, and leadership capabilities.

  • Build a strong security team and foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

  • Drive an AI-first approach across security engineering and operations, using AI tools and automation to improve efficiency, automate repetitive work, accelerate delivery, and enable the team to operate at greater scale.

  • Identify opportunities to apply AI across security engineering, detection, vulnerability management, testing, automation, and operational processes while maintaining appropriate security and governance controls.

  • Translate emerging AI and cloud security risks into clear strategy, priorities, and investments.

  • Establish clear ownership, accountability, and measurable security outcomes across the team.

Required Qualifications

  • Security Leadership: 12+ years in cybersecurity/security engineering, including 4+ years leading engineering or security teams. Experience managing distributed teams across India and the U.S. is strongly preferred.

  • Hands-On Security Engineering: Strong hands-on experience securing production environments and writing or reviewing security automation using Python, Terraform, or equivalent. You must be able to design, build, review, and challenge technical security solutions.

  • Application & Product Security: Proven experience securing enterprise-scale applications, including secure design reviews, threat modeling, vulnerability management, and remediation with Engineering teams. Experience with Python, Go, or Node.js is preferred.

  • Cloud & Infrastructure Security: Deep experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure, including Kubernetes/container security, cloud architecture, workload identity, and least-privilege access.

  • AI Security: Practical understanding of LLM and agentic AI security, including prompt injection, insecure output handling, excessive agency, tool abuse, and data exposure. Strong security fundamentals with demonstrated AI security experience or self-directed learning are valued.

  • Communication & Leadership: Ability to explain technical risk and security strategy to executives, customers, auditors, and engineering teams, while working effectively across global teams and time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a multi-tenant SaaS or AI platform company serving regulated enterprise customers (financial services, insurance, healthcare, or telecom).

  • Certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, or a cloud provider security certification.

  • Experience supporting enterprise customer security reviews, third-party risk assessments, or audit readiness.



Location preference:

India - Bangalore


Uniphore is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity in the workplace. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status, and other protected characteristics.

For more information on how Uniphore uses AI to unify—and humanize—every enterprise experience, please visit www.uniphore.com.

title: Product Manager – Data Science & Machine Learning

Product Discovery & Customer Understanding

Technical Product Management
  • Partner closely with Software Engineering and AI Engineering to define functional and non-functional requirements.
  • Define clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and product behaviors.
  • Work with technical teams on APIs, integrations, data flows, enterprise architecture, security, performance, and scalability requirements.
  • Understand technical dependencies and trade-offs sufficiently to make effective prioritization decisions.
  • Ensure products can integrate effectively within complex enterprise technology environments.
AI & Agentic Capabilities
  • Work with AI teams to identify where generative and agentic AI can create meaningful product value.
  • Define appropriate boundaries between predictive ML, deterministic business logic, human decision-making, and agentic AI.
  • Ensure AI capabilities are designed with appropriate controls, explainability, governance, and human oversight.
Delivery & Execution
  • Work closely with Engineering, Data Science, Design, and QA throughout delivery.
  • Own product backlog prioritization and release scope.
  • Manage dependencies and product decisions throughout development.
  • Define launch readiness and acceptance criteria.
  • Track product performance after release and use data and customer feedback to determine subsequent priorities.
Commercial & Go-to-Market Support
  • Partner with Business Development, Sales, and Presales on strategic customer opportunities.

  • Equip commercial teams with a clear understanding of product capabilities, positioning, and boundaries.
  • Support the definition and measurement of pilot and customer success criteria.

They should be able to sit with a business stakeholder and understand the problem being solved, work with Data Science to understand how intelligence can help solve it, collaborate with Engineering to turn that intelligence into a scalable product, and define how the resulting business impact will be measured.

title: Product Manager
description:
Zlayt AI is a litigation automation platform built exclusively for personal injury law. From demand letters and deposition summaries to discovery responses and case analysis, Zlayt equips law firms with intelligent tools that draft faster, think strategically, and deliver results without friction, setup, or compromise.

We're an early-stage, product-led company building the category-defining product for legal AI in a large, underserved niche. This is a rare opportunity to shape what the product becomes — working directly with the founding team, real PI lawyers, and real case data.


The Role

Zlayt AI is hiring a Product Manager to own the product from problem to shipped feature. You'll work directly with the founders and engineering to decide what we build, why, and in what order — then make sure it ships and actually works for the lawyers and legal assistants who use it every day.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's role. There is no product org to step into. You'll be writing the first specs, running the first structured discovery, and setting up how product decisions get made.


What You'll Do

  • Own the product roadmap: talk to PI lawyers and staff, find the highest-value workflow problems, and turn them into a prioritized plan
  • Write clear specs and acceptance criteria that engineers can build from without guesswork
  • Work hands-on with AI: define how features should behave, test outputs against real legal work product, and set the quality bar for what "good enough to ship" means
  • Run discovery and feedback loops with early customers, including Zinda Law Group as the first major client
  • Define and track the metrics that show whether a feature is working (adoption, time saved, output quality, retention)
  • Operate with significant ambiguity in an early-stage environment, making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting quickly


Who You Are

  • A builder, not an inheritor: You've shipped a 0-to-1 software product or major feature as the accountable PM — you know what it takes to build something from nothing, not just run an existing roadmap
  • Technical enough to be dangerous: You've worked directly with engineers day to day, can read a technical design, and don't need a translator to discuss APIs, data models, or model behavior
  • AI-native: You've shipped or worked hands-on with LLM or AI-powered features, and you use AI tools yourself to do your own work faster
  • Workflow-obsessed: You've built software for a demanding professional user — legal, healthcare, finance, or similar — where the details of the workflow decide whether the product gets used
  • Startup-tested: You've worked in small, fast-moving companies where you had to build process yourself, not step into one that already existed
  • Self-directed: Your track record shows work you personally drove — not just team results you were adjacent to
  • Experienced but still hands-on: Roughly 4–10 years of total professional experience, with at least 3 in product management
  • Stable but not stagnant: A track record of meaningful tenure at each stop, with job changes that make sense (promotions, acquisitions, layoffs, or clear career logic — not a pattern of short stints)


Our Philosophy

We firmly uphold the value of every individual within our team, ensuring they have the chance to build a rewarding career both financially and personally. Our firm's structure is designed to offer exceptional prospects for growth and advancement. At Zlayt AI, every team member leaves at the end of the day with the satisfaction of knowing they have diligently served our clients and positively impacted the lives of others. Join us and experience a remarkable work environment at our organization!

Zlayt AI is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or other protected status as required by applicable law.

title: Lead HPC Engineer
company: The Walter and Eliza Hall Institute
description:
The opportunity
At WEHI, computing power turns data into discoveries. Our researchers use Milton, our high performance computing environment, to analyse genomic, imaging and other large-scale data that is changing how we understand and treat cancer, infection and immune disease.

We're looking for a Lead HPC Engineer to be WEHI's technical authority for Milton. You'll keep it secure, reliable and well used today, and you'll lead the technical work to take WEHI to its next platform. Over the next three years WEHI will set a new compute and AI strategy, procure and build a new platform, and migrate every research workload onto it. You'll be at the centre of each step.

This is a hands-on role, you'll own the platform, work with other technical teams and see the results in the science.

What you'll do

  • Run Milton day to day: Slurm, NVIDIA GPU compute, VAST Data and Lenovo storage, Quantum StorNext and tape, and an NVIDIA Spectrum network fabric
  • Look after capacity, performance, patching, backup, and data centre power and cooling
  • Act as technical lead for WEHI's 2028+ Compute and AI Strategy: on-premises, hybrid or cloud
  • Lead the technical side of procuring and building the new platform, then migrating workloads to it
  • Automate with infrastructure-as-code, and document so knowledge is shared
  • Work with our Research Computing Platform team and researchers to get the most from HPC and AI

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years running Linux HPC or large-scale research computing infrastructure, ideally as the senior or lead engineer
  • Strong production Slurm administration
  • Experience with parallel or scale-out storage (VAST, Lustre, GPFS or StorNext)
  • GPU and CUDA stack experience, and an understanding of HPC networking (InfiniBand, RoCE or high-speed Ethernet)
  • Ansible or similar, plus Bash and Python
  • Research software environments: Apptainer, Spack, EasyBuild or Conda
  • The ability to explain technical trade-offs clearly to scientists, leaders and vendors

Experience with life science workloads, cloud HPC, AI inference platforms, or building a new HPC platform would be a real plus.

Why WEHI

  • Your work directly speeds up medical research
  • A rare chance to shape a platform from strategy through to cutover
  • Hybrid working from our Parkville campus

Terms of appointment
This position is an ongoing role in a full time capacity. Salary is Professional Services Employee Level 9 ($141,910 - $153,610). Very attractive salary packaging options are available for general living expenses, meal entertainment, novated leasing and more. 12% superannuation payable, plus up to a further 5% after the first 6 months of service via our matching superannuation scheme.

General enquiries can be directed to recruitment@wehi.edu.au. A position description is available here.

How to apply
Apply with your resume and a short cover letter outlining your HPC experience

Application Closing Date: The closing date for applications is 30 November 2026. However, we will be reviewing applications as they are received, and WEHI reserves the right to appoint a suitable candidate prior to the closing date. We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible to avoid missing this opportunity.

WEHI - Brighter together

WEHI is where the world's brightest minds collaborate and innovate to make discoveries that will help us to live healthier for longer. Our medical researchers have been serving the community for more than 100 years. We bring together people with different skills and experience who are committed to long-term discovery. Our teams of researchers are committed to solving the most complex health problems, making transformative discoveries for cancer, infectious and immune diseases, developmental disorders and healthy ageing.

WEHI is a place where people are able to shine. People who are inquisitive, who are committed, who are passionate. People who want to make a difference. And we are committed to ensuring they have the tools to flourish, personally and professionally. We are a community of researchers, students and professional service staff who work towards achieving discoveries that improve human health. We are driven by collaboration, curiosity and creativity. We are committed to making a positive difference to the lives of people in Australia and around the world. We are WEHI. We are brighter together.

WEHI's commitment to diversity and inclusion

At WEHI we strive to foster a flexible working environment that encourages individual differences and promotes collaboration and creativity. We recognise that talent does not sit within a single identifiable group in our society and that WEHI's ability to shape contemporary scientific thinking and deliver leading professional services relies on a diversity of thought within our organisation. Our action to promote gender equality has been recognised with an Athena SWAN Bronze Award from Science in Australia Gender Equity (SAGE) and we offer a range of support for women researchers.

Our commitment to celebrating diversity and addressing inequities is further demonstrated through our Diversity and Inclusion Strategy, Gender Action Plan, Reconciliation Action Plan and our WE-Pride network for LGBTQIA+ staff and students. We actively encourage applications from, people with a disability, culturally, religiously and linguistically diverse people and people with diverse genders and sexualities. Should you require support during the recruitment process due to special needs or consideration, please contact the People and Culture team.

WEHI's commitment to Indigenous employment

WEHI is working to create a future where Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples will be engaged at the scientific frontier, making exciting discoveries and decisions about the future of health in this country, and part of a leading professional services workforce supporting the realisation of these discoveries. We are committed to creating a culturally safe workplace and offering career development and leadership opportunities to First Nations staff and students. We strongly encourage any Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply.

title: Vertical Lead, Policy & National Security
description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Role: Vertical Technology Lead, Policy & National Security

Altana’s mission is to power a new era of globalization organized around trusted networks. Nowhere is that mission more consequential — or more demanding — than in the policy and national security community, where the questions our customers bring us are matters of sovereignty, security, and how a nation understands the networks it depends on.

These are the hardest programs we run. The technical bar is high and it keeps rising: the biggest opportunities are won, kept, and expanded on the strength of the technical work itself — sometimes on technical capability alone. As these engagements grow, so does the machinery large government partners expect from a serious partner: program management, delivery cadence, contractual rigor, accreditation. Left unmanaged, that machinery swamps the very people whose job is to architect and build.

We’re changing how we deliver so it doesn’t. Large and strategic accounts are staffed with dedicated Implementation Delivery Managers (IDMs) who carry the program, project, and delivery-management load — and, as an account grows more complex, we trade up the team to meet it. That frees the technical leadership of the vertical to do what only it can do: hold the architecture bar, win the technical argument, and drive the last mile of product where the mission needs something that doesn’t exist yet.

As Vertical Technology Lead for Policy & National Security, you own the technical outcomes for the vertical end-to-end. You are the senior technical counterpart to the vertical’s commercial leadership — setting the technical approach that wins business, owning the solution architecture and delivery that turns wins into mission outcomes, and leading the team that does the work. This is a UK-based leadership role operating in the national security context, working with classified missions and secured environments, in close partnership with our Platform Operations function and with core Engineering, Product & Design (EPD).

What You'll Do

  • Own the technical approach across the vertical's capture efforts. Give the commercial team the technical volumes, proposal content, and supporting material they need to win.
  • Partner with the Head of Vertical so what we sell delivers on what decision-makers and end users need. Bring technical credibility to the pitch when it counts.
  • Build and maintain relationships with key technology partners across the UK and allied national security ecosystem.
  • Advise commercial leadership on product-market fit and on whether proposed solution architectures can close known capability gaps.
  • Turn the vertical's needs into clear, cross-cutting product features and requests that matter most to customers and open the most pipeline

Own the Architecture & Delivery

  • Own the technical architecture and delivery for the vertical's accounts, from scoping through deployment (PaaS and SaaS). Hold the quality bar for performance, security, and maintainability across both the initial build and ongoing change, and lead day-to-day compliant operations.
  • Stand up and direct Implementation Delivery Managers (IDMs) on large and strategic accounts.
  • Staff accounts based on their complexity, and move your strongest people onto the highest-stakes accounts as they grow.
  • Work closely with EPD and core engineering to build solution designs, whether by configuring existing capabilities or developing new ones. Drive last-mile product development where the product doesn't yet do what the mission requires.
  • Own the vertical's customer support obligations. Build the process and technology that keep the field-to-product feedback loop running across every account.
  • Make sure the vertical's deployments meet Altana's security, risk, and compliance obligations in secured and regulated environments. Partner with Platform Operations on regulated-environment engineering and accreditation, while optimizing for scale and GTM realities.

Lead and Grow

  • Own hiring, staffing, and deployment for the vertical's technical delivery team.
  • Allocate resources across the vertical's accounts, concentrating technical talent where it matters most. Flag when headcount or product investment isn't matched to opportunity.
  • Develop your people through Altana's "capture-ground" model, giving more responsibility as they deliver. Support each person's path, whether that's technical mastery, running an account, or management.
  • Hold the technical quality bar, manage performance, and model technical product excellence.
  • Carry team culture and hold the team to the operating rhythm and communication standards, starting with our commitment to meeting contractual obligations.

Who You Are

You’ve delivered at the sharp end of the public sector. You’ve led complex technical programs for government — ideally in defence, intelligence, or national security — and you’re at home with mission owners and senior decision-makers, translating fluently between mission language and technical language.

You’re an architect who has also run delivery. You can own a solution architecture across SaaS and regulated environments, and you know the difference between owning the architecture and running the program. You’ve seen delivery-management overhead swallow good engineers, and you’ve built the muscle — and the team structure — to keep both moving.

You build teams and trade up as the mission grows. You staff to complexity, put the right people on the right accounts, and aren’t precious about changing the lineup when the technical bar rises.

You win on technical capability. You’ve turned technical credibility into expansion — surfacing where the platform can unlock new mission value and partnering with commercial to convert it, without needing to own the number yourself.

You operate in secured environments. You’re experienced handling sensitive and classified data, and you understand what it takes to deliver software inside accredited, controlled environments.

You lead through inspiration. You set a high bar, grow the people around you, and bring a team along on hard, ambiguous problems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 12+ years of technical experience spanning enterprise/solution architecture, deployment, and product development, including leading technical teams and complex, customer-facing deployments end-to-end.
  • Deep public sector experience, ideally in defence, intelligence, or national security.
  • Solution architecture depth across cloud (AWS or Azure), data engineering (Python, SQL, Spark, Databricks), complex system integrations (REST APIs, SSO/SAML), and containerized deployments (Kubernetes, Docker).
  • A track record partnering with commercial teams on pre-sales, capture, and expansion — turning clearly-defined customer outcomes into technical product specs and a credible delivery path.
  • People-leadership experience: hiring, growing, and holding the bar for a team of technical delivery staff.
  • UK-based, with the right to work in the United Kingdom, and able to work on-site with customers as the mission requires.
  • Hold, or are eligible and willing to obtain, UK Security Check (SC) clearance — existing SC (or higher, e.g. DV) is a strong plus.

This role is based in the United Kingdom (London) with hybrid work flexibility. Candidates must be within commuting distance of our London hub.

The recruiter assigned to this role can share more information about the specific compensation and benefit details associated with this role during the hiring process.

Our Values

Our values are the core beliefs that shape who we are, what we stand for, and how we behave.They form the foundation of Altana’s culture and integrity and guide how we hire, design, build, and connect with each other and our customers.

  • Trust: Our customers and partners entrust us with missions of the highest importance. We honor that by keeping our word, meeting commitments, and ensuring every action we take reinforces confidence in us. We rely on each other to deliver, to speak openly, and to hold ourselves accountable.
  • Resilience: In a world of uncertainty and complexity, our work must withstand challenges, evolve with conditions, and ensure reliability over time. Resilience is both how we operate and what we deliver. It’s how we respond when things don’t go to plan –– we adapt, we support each other, and we keep moving forward.
  • Stewardship: We are stewards of every mission we touch. Because our work impacts lives and futures, we hold ourselves accountable to delivering mission impact and never compromising. Our responsibility extends beyond individual projects to the broader system of global trade. We believe that stewardship starts from within so that we can bring focus, creativity, and excellence to our work. Senior Director, Customer Innovation

About the Role

  • Formulate and deliver an end-to-end macro strategy encompassing Sales Engineering Labs, COE, and Forward Engineering teams with clear, outcome-oriented milestones.

  • Partner with Worldwide Sales Leadership to explicitly define, audit, and document field requirements for specialist sales engineering resources versus territory sales engineers.
  • Present data-driven business cases highlighting the strategic necessity, ROI, and resource scaling of each specialist function ahead of annual planning cycles.
  • Maintain a highly visible executive presence in high-stakes corporate settings, driving cross-functional alignment and navigating organizational change.

The Skills and Qualities You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of experience leading technical sales or systems engineering teams within cybersecurity, with at least 4+ years managing multi-tiered organizations (managing managers).
  • Demonstrated technical operations mastery, with proven experience overseeing complex technical infrastructure groups such as Cloud/On-Prem Demo Labs, Centers of Excellence, or Technical Enablement functions.
  • High conceptual familiarity with Forward Engineering and systems architecture, including API ecosystems, security orchestration (SOAR), technology integrations, and enterprise security platforms.
  • Strong financial and operational acumen, with experience structuring headcount models, proving ROI on technical overhead, and mapping engineering performance to revenue attainment metrics.
  • High-stakes mediation skills and self-awareness to manage conflict, adapt to challenging group dynamics, and maintain an active, commanding leadership voice under pressure.
  • Ability to think big and act small — breaking massive organizational goals into time-bound milestones, executing rapidly, and pivoting effectively based on business metrics.

title: FoDM - Country Insights Business Partner (10 positions)
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

The global Insights function empowers affiliates and global leadership with deep market intelligence, competitive analysis, customer understanding, and commercial analytics. Combining centralized data capabilities, advanced analytics, and strategic advisory, the team delivers evidence-based decision support to drive commercial planning, resource allocation, and sustained business growth across diverse healthcare markets.


As the Country Insights Partner, you serve as the primary insights interface for assigned affiliates, operating with a direct affiliate-level scope of impact on commercial planning and marketing investment decisions, while driving indirect global impact through the quality of field intelligence fed back to global teams. In this role, your time is balanced between strategic initiatives (approximately 60% focused on business planning support, competitive advisory, insight synthesis, and multi-year to annual recommendations) and operational execution (approximately 40% focused on regular report production, data product adoption, and research coordination).


The Opportunity


  • Analysis & Insights Generation (~35%): Develop and deliver regular market and competitive reports for assigned affiliates by combining global data sources with local market knowledge; monitor and analyze competitor activity, product launches, pricing moves, and market access developments; conduct affiliate-specific analyses (local competitive assessments, market sizing, opportunity identification) using available data sources and tools; and provide affiliate leadership with timely, contextualized updates on market dynamics affecting commercial performance.
  • Insight Synthesis & Decision Support (~25%): Partner with affiliate Strategic Marketing Leads and commercial leadership to support business planning with evidence-based market context and recommendations; synthesize intelligence across domains (market trends, customer feedback, campaign performance) to identify opportunities and blind spots; participate in affiliate planning cycles, commercial reviews, and launch readiness assessments as the insights representative; and advise on areas warranting further investigation by connecting affiliates to the right global specialist when deeper analytical work is required.
  • Data Capture & Local Intelligence (~20%): Collect local field intelligence, competitor signals, and customer feedback from affiliate stakeholders and commercial teams; identify market dynamics not visible in global data (emerging competitors, regulatory changes, tender dynamics, customer behavior shifts); feed local insights back to global teams for incorporation into global reporting and product development; channel affiliate requirements to global teams for prioritization; and maintain awareness of relevant local data vendors and syndicated sources to advise the global vendor and partner management capability on local data buying priorities and recommend new sources where gaps exist.
  • Insights Dissemination & Enablement (~20%): Drive adoption of global data products, dashboards, and insight tools across assigned affiliates; educate affiliate stakeholders on available insight products and support their effective use; provide feedback to global teams on product relevance, usability, and gaps based on affiliate experience; and build visibility of the Insights function's value to establish yourself as a trusted advisor.
  • Cross-Functional & Global Collaboration: Connect affiliates to the right global resources for commercial and account-related analytics needs, collaborating closely with Insights Business Specialists (who provide analytical and research support to help deliver against affiliate priorities) and engaging the CoE Subchapter Lead (line manager), Global Strategic Insights Leads, Insights Solution Managers & Leads, Advanced Analytics, and fellow Country Insights Business Partners for regional coordination and pattern sharing.
  • Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory: Act as an individual contributor (with no direct reports) solving varied, semi-structured, and cross-functional business problems; regularly interact with and influence affiliate Strategic Marketing Leads and Solution Marketing Leads; support Product Leads/Managers with competitive product-level intelligence and tender dynamics; handle bespoke requests for General/Country Managers; and deliver periodic presentations to affiliate leadership teams to communicate critical market dynamics.
  • Budgetary Influence: While this role does not directly own a budget—as research and data product budgets are managed centrally at the chapter and subchapter level—you directly influence the prioritization of research spend and data procurement through affiliate requirement articulation.

Who You Are


  • Education & Formal Training: Bachelor's degree required in business, marketing, life sciences, economics, or a quantitative discipline; Master's degree (MBA, MSc) or equivalent preferred.
  • Industry & Affiliate Experience: 5 to 8 years (depending on market assignment and specific position) of progressive experience in market research, competitive intelligence, commercial analytics, or a related function within the diagnostics, life sciences, or medtech industry; strong understanding of the IVD market, healthcare systems, and laboratory workflows; and preferred experience working in or with affiliate/country-level commercial organizations.
  • Analytical & Strategic Acumen: Proven track record of independently conducting market and competitive analyses, producing actionable reports, interpreting dashboards, statistical outputs, and market models, and understanding how insights drive business planning, marketing investment decisions, and commercial outcomes.
  • Communication & Stakeholder Management: Exceptional insight communication and executive presence to distill complex data into clear narratives for senior commercial audiences (both written and verbal); proven ability to advise and constructively challenge business leadership in a matrixed environment across diverse cultures and varying business practices.
  • Tools & Languages: Proficiency with market research platforms, BI/visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI), and standard business applications; excellent written and spoken English required, with local language proficiency required depending on the assigned market context.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.
